subject: [PATCH 0/3] perf/core: Fix software event sample data, then stop zeroing it

reviews.author: Peter Zijlstra
reviews.summary: Peter Zijlstra noted that the patch only partially addresses the issue of zeroing perf_sample_data in do_perf_sw_event(), and suggested that the code should be made consistent by applying the same fix to other places where this struct is used.

reviews.author: Peter Zijlstra
reviews.summary: The reviewer, Peter Zijlstra, suggested that the patch to stop zeroing perf_sample_data in do_perf_sw_event() should be a separate patch from the rest of the series.

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed Peter Zijlstra's concern that perf_tp_event(), perf_bp_event() and perf_swevent_hrtimer() might not be initializing perf_sample_data correctly, by explaining that these functions do call perf_sample_data_init() for each event and only use the sample ID fields. The author also acknowledged that these functions need the fix in patch 2 to work.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks! I went through the below. perf_tp_event(), perf_bp_event()
and perf_swevent_hrtimer() call perf_sample_data_init() for each event,
like do_perf_sw_event() does. The side-band emitters only use the
sample ID fields, which perf_event_header__init() writes and
perf_event__output_id_sample() reads under the same sample_id_all
check. So they are all fine to do.

But they do need the fix in patch 2 to work.

There is another fix that I found looking at your next reply.
Would you like me to send all the fixes and you can then send
the below patch (and the next one?)

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_STRUCT still leaks stack contents and agreed to add a fix for it in the form of a separate patch (e662f8539ca00096db3ee4d570efe97767427fbe) which writes var3_w as well.
reviews.raw_body:
Agreed, but IBS is not safe yet. For PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_STRUCT,
perf_ibs_parse_ld_st_data() writes only var1_dw and var2_w but sets
PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_TYPE, so perf_output_sample() copies var3_w from
whatever is on the stack. INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO hides that today, and
INIT_STACK_NONE kernels have leaked those 2 bytes since 6b2ae4952ef8.
With __uninitialized in perf_ibs_handle_irq() every kernel would.

We need the below:

commit e662f8539ca00096db3ee4d570efe97767427fbe
Author: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
Date:   Fri Nov 20 09:04:13 2026 -0800

    perf/x86/amd/ibs: Don't leak stack contents through PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_STRUCT

    For a load that missed the data cache, perf_ibs_parse_ld_st_data()
    reports the miss latency as the sample weight and marks
    PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_TYPE as done, so perf_prepare_sample() leaves the
    field alone. With PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_STRUCT it writes only var1_dw and
    var2_w, but perf_output_sample() copies all 8 bytes of the union into
    the ring buffer. var3_w therefore carries whatever was left in the
    on-stack struct perf_sample_data in perf_ibs_handle_irq().

    CONFIG_INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO hides this by clearing the struct on entry.
    Without it, every such sample hands 2 bytes of kernel stack to user
    space. "perf mem record" asks for PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_STRUCT on x86, and
    since v6.14 swfilt lets an unprivileged user sample their own tasks with
    IBS.

    Write var3_w as well.

    Fixes: 6b2ae4952ef8 ("perf/x86/amd: Support PERF_SAMPLE_{WEIGHT|WEIGHT_STRUCT}")
    Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
    Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>

diff --git a/arch/x86/events/amd/ibs.c b/arch/x86/events/amd/ibs.c
index 66e67e27224f18..9aa47751b37f6c 100644
--- a/arch/x86/events/amd/ibs.c
+++ b/arch/x86/events/amd/ibs.c
@@ -1376,6 +1376,7 @@ static void perf_ibs_parse_ld_st_data(__u64 sample_type,
                if (sample_type & PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT_STRUCT) {
                        data->weight.var1_dw = op_data3.dc_miss_lat;
                        data->weight.var2_w = op_data.tag_to_ret_ctr;
+                       data->weight.var3_w = 0;
                } else if (sample_type & PERF_SAMPLE_WEIGHT) {
                        data->weight.full = op_data3.dc_miss_lat;
                }


The other sites look fine to me, including arch-PEBS: the drain skips
records whose first fragment has no basic group, so var3_w is always
written there.

2026-11-20.patch_summary: This patch series fixes two bugs in the Linux kernel's perf/core module related to software event sample data. The first bug, present since v6.3, occurs when a sampling event inherits an uninitialized sample ID and timestamp from a previous event, causing issues with concurrent 'perf record' sessions. The second bug, introduced in v6.1, allows BPF programs to read uninitialized stack contents through the bpf_perf_event_data::addr field. The patches initialize the struct for each matching event, prevent BPF programs from reading uninitialized data, and stop zero-initializing the struct in do_perf_sw_event(). These changes improve performance by reducing the time it takes to handle context switches.

reviews.author: tip-bot2 Arif
reviews.summary: Reviewer Arif noted that the perf_swevent_match() function's 'data' argument is unused and requested it be dropped, while also initializing the struct perf_sample_data for each matching event to prevent sample ID reuse across software events.

reviews.author: tip-bot2 Arif
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the patch does not address the issue of BPF programs reading uninitialized sample addresses in perf_sample_data, and suggested clearing the address before running the program if nobody filled it in.
reviews.raw_body:
The following commit has been merged into the perf/urgent branch of tip:

Commit-ID:     91a18ff192c68329fcfdd4ed0a6d37dcac45ef50
Gitweb:        https://git.kernel.org/tip/91a18ff192c68329fcfdd4ed0a6d37dcac45ef50
Author:        Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
AuthorDate:    Thu, 19 Nov 2026 13:10:45 -08:00
Committer:     Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>
CommitterDate: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:09:06 +01:00

perf/core: Don't let BPF programs read an uninitialized sample address

A BPF program attached to a perf event gets a struct
bpf_perf_event_data, and reading its addr field turns into a load from
the perf_sample_data the sample is being assembled in. The verifier
allows that load no matter which fields the event samples.

perf_sample_data_init() used to store the address unconditionally, so
the program read 0 when there was none. To touch fewer cachelines, it
now stores the address only when it is non-zero, and
perf_prepare_sample() fills it in only when the event samples it
(PERF_SAMPLE_ADDR, PHYS_ADDR or DATA_PAGE_SIZE). For all other events,
including context switches, cpu-clock and hardware counters like
cycles, the program reads whatever was left in that stack slot, often a
kernel pointer.

Kernels built with CONFIG_INIT_STACK_ALL_ZERO, the default when the
compiler supports it, mostly hide this by clearing the struct on
function entry. With INIT_STACK_ALL_PATTERN the program reads the fill
pattern instead.

Clear the address before running the program if nobody filled it in,
the same way the SIGTRAP path already checks PERF_SAMPLE_ADDR before
using it. Events without a BPF program are not affected.

Fixes: 7b0846301531 ("perf: Use sample_flags for addr")
Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20261119211235.99805-3-usama.arif@linux.dev
---
 kernel/events/core.c | 3 +++
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+)

diff --git a/kernel/events/core.c b/kernel/events/core.c
index 42bd8ad..ee51134 100644
--- a/kernel/events/core.c
+++ b/kernel/events/core.c
@@ -10819,6 +10819,9 @@ static int bpf_overflow_handler(struct perf_event *event,
 	prog = READ_ONCE(event->prog);
 	if (prog) {
 		perf_prepare_sample(data, event, regs);
+		/* bpf_perf_event_data::addr is readable without PERF_SAMPLE_ADDR */
+		if (!(data->sample_flags & PERF_SAMPLE_ADDR))
+			data->addr = 0;
 		ret = bpf_prog_run(prog, &ctx);
 	}
 	rcu_read_unlock();

reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a BPF program is attached to a perf event and tries to read the addr field of bpf_perf_event_data without PERF_SAMPLE_ADDR being set, which can result in reading kernel pointers. reviews.author: tip-bot2 Arif
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the patch does not properly initialize perf_sample_data for each matching software event, leading to a potential data corruption issue where a sampling event later in the list emits sample IDs and timestamp prepared for an earlier one, causing the kernel to write past its ring-buffer reservation over the records that follow. The reviewer suggested initializing the struct for each matching event by calling perf_sample_data_init() before passing it to perf_swevent_event().

reviews.author: tip-bot2 Zijlstra
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the patch to mark perf_sample_data as __uninitialized is an optimization, but they requested clarification on whether this change actually reduces code size or improves performance.

reviews.author: tip-bot2 Arif
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the memset of perf_sample_data in do_perf_sw_event() is unnecessary and expensive, as its contents are copied into a ring buffer that userspace maps, and every field must be written before it's read. They suggested marking the struct __uninitialized to indicate this.

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the swapoff path needs to drop the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(), agreed to restructure in v2, but did not provide a clear resolution signal.
